newsitem.title: ANGOLA: UNHCR in Angola plans for possible Zaire influx.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR in Angola plans for possible Zaire influx.

text.p: The office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Angola said on Tuesday it was developing contingency plans in case of a possible influx of refugees from neighbouring Zaire.
Deputy UNHCR representative in Angola Peter de Clerco told Reuters the agency was reinforcing its relief stocks. There was no sign yet of a possible influx to Angola, Zaire's southern neighbour.
More than a million refugees in eastern Zaire face a threat of famine after Tutsi rebels seized a string of towns along Zaire's border with Rwanda and Burundi.
"We are in the process of making contingency plans and reinforcing our relief items stocks. This is purely for planning purposes.
"The possible influx of refugees from Zaire is one of the scenarios we have looked at in our country plan because of the fluid nature of things there," de Clerco said.
Angola has its own refugee problems to deal with after two decades of civil war between government and former rebel UNITA forces, and is in the process of rebuilding the country.

The UNHCR has overseen the repatriation of 35,650 Angolans of an estimated 330,000 refugees who fled to Zambia and Zaire during the last years of fighting until 1994 when UNITA and the government signed a peace accord to end the war.

"The number of (Angolan) returnees have been far less than we expected and so we have at any rate additional stocks available," de Clerco said adding that increased fighting in Zaire could see Angolans in that country returning home quicker.
